# TestScript for 30-config-loader — the programmatic configuration document.
# The conga.ConfigLoader hook builds the config tier in code: --profile selects
# a stored profile whose values bind at the config rank with --why origins,
# and the prod profile carries the force-all feature gate.

# 1. The default dev profile supplies host, port, and headers from the document.
exec deploy
stdout '--host\s+string\s+dev\.example\.com\s+● config host'
stdout '--port\s+int\s+7100\s+● config port'
stdout '--headers\s+map\[string\]string\s+X-Region=eu\s+● config headers'
stdout 'connect dev\.example\.com:7100 headers=1 force-all=false'

# 2. Command-line values outrank the document.
exec deploy --host cli.example.com
stdout '--host\s+string\s+cli\.example\.com\s+● cli --host'

# 3. The prod profile carries the force-all gate: the gated flag appears and is
#    usable, while the dev profile gates it off (exit 2).
exec deploy --profile prod
stdout '--profile\s+string\s+prod\s+● cli --profile'
stdout 'connect prod\.example\.com:7200 headers=2 force-all=true'
exec deploy --profile prod --force-all
stdout 'connect prod\.example\.com:7200 headers=2 force-all=true'
exit-status 2 deploy --force-all
stderr 'flag .--force-all. requires feature "force-all"'

# 4. An unknown profile fails the loader: app-authored data is a runtime error
#    (exit 1), never a usage error.
exit-status 1 deploy --profile staging
stderr 'config loader failed: unknown profile "staging"'

# 5. --why attributes document values to their origin labels.
exec deploy --profile prod --why
stdout 'config \(profile prod\)'
stdout 'profile prod\s+loaded: profile prod'
